content: 1. Carmona S, Bor J, Nattey C, Maughan-Brown B, Maskew M, Fox MP, and colleagues conducted a study highlighting the persistent high burden of advanced HIV disease among patients seeking care in South Africa's national HIV program. This research utilized data from a nationwide laboratory cohort and was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018. 2. Thomson KA, Hughes J, Baeten JM, John-Stewart G, Celum C, Cohen CR, and colleagues analyzed the increased risk of HIV acquisition among women during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Their prospective per-coital-act analysis focused on women with HIV-infected partners and was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2018. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a progress report in 2015 on the global health sector response to HIV from 2000 to 2015, emphasizing innovations in Africa. 4. In 2014, the WHO published a global update on the health sector response to HIV, providing insights into progress and challenges. 5. Nglazi M, Zunza M, Mtathhews C, Low N, and Young T conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine effective partner notification strategies for sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. Their findings were presented at the joint meeting of the 23rd ISSTDR and 20th IUSTI in Vancouver, Canada, in 2019. 6. Hensen B, Taoka S, Lewis JJ, Weiss HA, and Hargreaves J systematically reviewed strategies to increase men's HIV testing in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2014. 7. Stankard P, Groves A, Jamil MS, Baggaley R, and Johnson C conducted a systematic review of community-based HIV testing in general and key populations. This report was published by the WHO in 2019. 8. Wagner A, Njuguna I, Escudero J, Burke R, Obermeyer C, Neary J, and colleagues explored demand creation strategies to improve HIV testing uptake. Their findings were published by the WHO in 2019. 9. Hayes RJ, Donnell D, Floyd S, Mandla N, Bwalya J, Sabapathy K, and colleagues evaluated the effect of universal testing and treatment on HIV incidence in the HPTN 071 (PopART) study. Their results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 10. Hauck K analyzed the cost and societal value of household-based combination HIV prevention interventions implemented in the HPTN 071 (PopART) study. This research was presented at the 10th International AIDS Conference on Science in Mexico City, Mexico, in 2019. 11. Gaolathe T, Wirth KE, Holme MP, Makhema J, Moyo S, Chakalisa U, and colleagues assessed Botswana's progress toward achieving the 2020 UNAIDS 90-90-90 goals for antiretroviral therapy and virological suppression. Their population-based survey was published in The Lancet HIV in 2016. 12. Havlir DV, Balzer LB, Charlebois ED, Clark TD, Kwarisiima D, Ayeiko J, and colleagues investigated HIV testing and treatment using a community health approach in rural Africa. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 13. Sabapathy K, Van den Bergh R, Fidler S, Hayes R, and Ford N conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the uptake of home-based voluntary HIV testing in sub-Saharan Africa. Their study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2012. 14. Dalal S, Johnson C, Fonner V, Kennedy CE, Siegfried N, Figueroa C, and colleagues examined the impact of assisted partner notification services on improving HIV test uptake and case finding. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2017. 15. The International Labour Organization (ILO) published a report in 2018 on the global estimates of the impact of HIV and AIDS on the world of work. 16. The WHO and ILO jointly published a report in 2018 on HIV self-testing in the workplace. 17. Johnson CC, Kennedy C, Fonner V, Siegfried N, Figueroa C, Dalal S, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing the effects of HIV self-testing to standard HIV testing services. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2017. 18. Sharma M, Smith JA, Farquhar C, Ying R, Cherutich P, Golden M, and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of assisted partner notification services for reducing HIV burden in western Kenya. Their study was published in AIDS in 2018. 19. Phillips AN, Cambiano V, Nakagawa F, Bansi-Matharu L, Wilson D, Jani I, and colleagues proposed cost-per-diagnosis as a metric for monitoring the cost-effectiveness of HIV testing programs in low-income settings in southern Africa. Their health economic and modeling analysis was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 20. Cambiano V, Johnson CC, Hatzold K, Terris-Prestholt F, Maheswaran H, Thirumurthy H, and colleagues analyzed the impact and cost-effectiveness of community-based HIV self-testing in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 21. The WHO and UNAIDS announced recommendations from an expert consultation on male circumcision for HIV prevention in 2007. 22. The WHO published guidance on provider-initiated HIV testing and counseling in health facilities in 2007. 23. UNICEF released a report in 2018 on HIV prevention for and with adolescent and young key populations. 24. Hosek S and Pettifor A reviewed HIV prevention interventions for adolescents in Current HIV/AIDS Reports in 2019. 25. The WHO published recommendations on adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights in 2018. 26. The WHO and UNAIDS released global standards for quality health-care services for adolescents in 2015. 27. Ahmed K, Baeten JM, Beksinska M, Bekker LG, Bukusi EA, Donnell D, and colleagues conducted a randomized, multicenter, open-label trial to assess HIV incidence among women using various contraceptive methods. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2019. 28. The WHO published guidelines on HIV disclosure counseling for children up to 12 years of age in 2011. 29. Clark JL, Long CM, Giron JM, Cuadros JA, Caceres CF, Coates TJ, and colleagues studied partner notification for sexually transmitted diseases in Peru, focusing on knowledge, attitudes, and practices in a high-risk community. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2007. 30. Clark JL, Perez-Brumer A, Salazar X explored partner notification, partner management, and conceptual frameworks for HIV/STI control among MSM in Peru. Their study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2015. 31. Tan WS and Chio TW conducted a patient preference survey at the national STI clinic in Singapore to determine preferred partner notification methods. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2015. 32. The WHO reviewed national HIV testing policies in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the age of consent for HIV testing, in 2019. 33. Quinn C, Wong V, Jamil M, Baggaley R, and Johnson C reviewed symptomand risk-based screening tools to optimize provider-initiated HIV testing and counseling in highand low-HIV-burden settings. Their findings were published by the WHO in 2019. 34. Fox K, Ferguson J, and Ajose W reviewed current policies and issues related to adolescent consent for HIV testing in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published by the WHO in 2013. 35. The WHO published guidance in 2013 on HIV testing and counseling and care for adolescents living with HIV, providing recommendations for a public health approach. 36. Korenromp EL, Rowley J, Alonso M, Mello MB, Wijesooriya NS, Mahiane SG, and colleagues estimated the global burden of maternal and congenital syphilis and associated adverse birth outcomes for 2016. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2019. 37. The WHO released a global hepatitis report in 2017. 38. The WHO published a progress report in 2019 on HIV, viral hepatitis, and sexually transmitted infections. 39. The WHO released an information note in 2017 on the use of dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests. 40. Ishikawa N, Dalal S, Johnson C, Hogan DR, Shimbo T, Shaffer N, and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of universal antenatal HIV testing compared to focused approaches across various HIV prevalence settings. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2016. 41. Meisner J, Rodriguez P, Roberts A, Barnabas R, Newman-Owiredu M, Taylor M, and colleagues modeled the cost-effectiveness of dual maternal HIV and syphilis testing and retesting strategies in highand low-HIV-prevalence countries. Their findings were published by the WHO in 2019. 42. The WHO published consolidated guidelines in 2016 on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection. 43. The WHO released guidelines in 2017 for managing advanced HIV disease and the rapid initiation of antiretroviral therapy. 44. The WHO published guidance in 2017 on preventing HIV during pregnancy and breastfeeding in the context of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). 45. Kumar AM, Gupta D, Kumar A, Gupta RS, Kanchar A, Rao R, and colleagues conducted operational research in India to implement routine HIV testing among patients with presumptive tuberculosis. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2016. 46. The WHO released consolidated guidelines in 2016 on integrating collaborative TB and HIV services within a comprehensive care package for people who inject drugs. 47. The WHO published guidance in 2018 on family-based index case testing to identify children with HIV. 48. The WHO released a series in 2007 on the effectiveness of interventions to address HIV in prisons. 49. The WHO published consolidated guidelines in 2019 on the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women living with HIV. 50. The WHO released guidelines in 2017 on hepatitis B and C testing. 51. The WHO updated recommendations in 2019 on firstand second-line antiretroviral regimens. 52. Newell M, Coovadia H, Cortina-Borja M, Rollins N, Gaillard P, Dabis F, and colleagues conducted a pooled analysis of mortality among infected and uninfected infants born to HIV-infected mothers in Africa. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2004. 53. The WHO published an HIV molecular diagnostics toolkit in 2019 to improve access to viral load testing and infant diagnosis. 54. The WHO released public health guidance in 2017 on quality HIV testing in the context of antiretroviral drugs. 55. The WHO published a Country Intelligence Database in 2019. 56. Olaru ID, McHugh G, Dakshina S, Majonga E, Dauya E, Bandason T, and colleagues reported false-negative HIV tests using oral fluid tests in children on antiretroviral therapy in Harare, Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2017. 57. Were WA, Mermin JH, Wamai N, Awor AC, Bechange S, Moss S, and colleagues studied undiagnosed HIV infection and couple HIV discordance among household members of HIV-infected individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy in Uganda. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2006. 58. The WHO published a strategic framework in 2018 for planning, introducing, and scaling up HIV self-testing. 59. Morton JF, Celum C, Njoroge J, Nakyanzi A, Wakhungu I, Tindimwebwa E, and colleagues developed a counseling framework for HIV-serodiscordant couples on the integrated use of antiretroviral therapy and pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2017. 60. The WHO published guidance in 2012 on couples HIV testing and counseling, including antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples. 61. The WHO released clinical and policy guidelines in 2013 on responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. 62. The WHO published a clinical handbook in 2014 on health care for women subjected to intimate partner violence or sexual violence. 63. The WHO released clinical guidelines in 2017 on responding to children and adolescents who have been sexually abused. 64. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published public health guidance in 2018 on screening and vaccination for infectious diseases in newly arrived migrants within the EU/EEA. 65. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees published guidelines in 2014 on delivering antiretroviral therapy to migrants and crisis-affected persons in sub-Saharan Africa.
